title: Process Execution via String Template Commands
platform_conditions: Kotlin/JVM semantics over java.lang.Runtime / java.lang.ProcessBuilder; applies on server JVM and Android runtime (Runtime.exec available since API level 1)
security_mechanism: Runtime.getRuntime().exec(String) tokenizes the whole command line with StringTokenizer (whitespace splitting, no shell quoting rules), so a value containing spaces or shell metacharacters either breaks into extra argv elements or — when the string is passed through 'sh -c' — is interpreted by the shell with full metacharacter semantics (';', '|', '$(...)'). Kotlin string templates make this splice invisible at the call site: "sh -c $cmd" looks like one fixed command while $cmd contributes the actual program. Argument injection also occurs without a shell when an input starting with '-' becomes an option of the launched program.

source_sink_clues.source: Deep-link/Intent parameters, exported-component extras, or server-side request data that reach the executed command string or an argv element.
source_sink_clues.sink: Runtime.getRuntime().exec with a template or concatenated string, ProcessBuilder with a single shell string, and any exec wrapped in 'sh -c' or 'su -c'

tracking_guards: Check the process is started with ProcessBuilder and an argv list with a fixed executable and the dynamic value as one element (never through a shell); if a shell is unavoidable, verify quoting/escaping and strict allowlist validation of the value; check '-'-prefixed inputs cannot reach a program that parses options (positional separator '--' or validation).
not_candidate_when: The command is a fixed constant with no interpolation, the dynamic value is one argv element to a program that takes no options, or the value is validated against a strict allowlist grammar that excludes metacharacters before the call.
public_references: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/78.html
